You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.

=== REVIEW FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] `Last-Modified` is deleted on 304 (etag.go `h.Del("Last-Modified")`). Criterion 4 says the 304 keeps other headers and drops only Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding. Reproduced with a real server: handler sets `Last-Modified`, request has `If-None-Match: *`, 304 arrives with `Last-Modified=""`. Note that Go's `writeNotModified` does the same when an ETag is present, so this is parity with net/http, but it contradicts the criterion's literal list. The orchestrator must decide whether to keep the criterion or the parity.
- [minor] Panic after buffered writes under `ETag` outer and `Recoverer` inner yields 200 with the partial body and a computed ETag. Not reproduced as a regression: a plain net/http baseline gives the same 200 "partial", so this is not caused by the diff.
- [minor] Handler setting `ETag` to `""` gets a computed tag instead of an empty one. Behaviour is reasonable, but the criterion's "handler did not set an ETag" is ambiguous here. Not reproduced as a failure.

Reply exactly:
{"found": "yes"|"no", "finding_quote": "<verbatim quote of the matching finding, or empty>", "blocking": "yes"|"no"}
"blocking" is "yes" only if the matching finding is tagged [blocking].
